algorithm.Title: Scrapes - Female (Adult)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Adult | Female
Definition: Scrape/graze assessment decomposed from NHS.UK's published cuts and grazes guidance.

Background.ExpertReviewer: PENDING: Qatar adult, pediatric, obstetric, emergency, specialty, and nursing governance review

FirstAid: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive. Apply continuous firm direct pressure with a clean cloth or dressing; add further dressings without removing soaked layers. Do not remove an embedded object or press directly on it. Keep the person still and warm. If unresponsive and not breathing normally, start age-appropriate CPR as directed by 999. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Is this a deep, gaping, or actively bleeding cut rather than a superficial scrape or graze?
questions.Information: A deep cut or laceration belongs in the Cuts and Lacerations pathway.

questions.Question: Is bleeding heavy, spurting, or not controlled by firm direct pressure; is there an embedded object, exposed bone/tendon, loss of feeling or movement, a pale/cold limb, major trauma, or reduced consciousness?
questions.Information: A reported scrape may conceal a deeper wound, major bleeding, neurovascular injury, fracture, or serious associated trauma.

questions.Question: Does the wound have soil, pus, or body fluids in it or is it still dirty after cleaning, or is it swollen/red/getting more painful with pus, or larger than about 5cm?
questions.Information: NHS.UK cuts and grazes guidance lists these as reasons to seek urgent clinical review.

questions.Question: For a child or vulnerable person, is the explanation absent, unsuitable, inconsistent with the wound or developmental ability, is there delay in seeking help or concern about supervision, might the caregiver be unsafe, or can the patient not be offered a safe opportunity to speak privately?
questions.Information: NICE child-maltreatment guidance identifies unsuitable or inconsistent explanations, possible neglect/lack of supervision, and caregiver obstruction of private discussion as safeguarding alerts. Exact Qatar reporting, destination, confidentiality, and disconnect actions remain GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED.

questions.Question: Is this a small, clean scrape with none of the features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance describes minor scrapes as manageable at home with basic first aid.

advice.Title: Qatar emergency wound response
Content: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive. Apply continuous firm direct pressure with a clean cloth or dressing; add further dressings without removing soaked layers. Do not remove an embedded object or press directly on it. Keep the person still and warm. If unresponsive and not breathing normally, start age-appropriate CPR as directed by 999. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: uncontrolled or spurting bleeding; pale, cold, confused, faint, or unresponsive person; loss of movement, feeling, or circulation.

advice.Title: Urgent scrape wound review
Content: Rinse superficial contamination gently with clean running water, cover with a clean non-stick dressing, and arrange same-day in-person review. Do not scrub deeply, probe, close, or remove embedded material. Tetanus and blood/body-fluid exposure actions require immunization history and the approved Qatar pathway.
Call Back If: increasing redness, swelling, pain, pus, red streaking, or fever; foreign material remains; bite, puncture, or body-fluid exposure.

advice.Title: Child wound safeguarding response
Content: Arrange urgent in-person clinical and safeguarding assessment through the Qatar governance-approved pathway. Offer the child a safe opportunity to speak privately when clinically and developmentally appropriate; do not rely on or disclose the plan to a caregiver who may be unsafe. Do not confront a suspected abuser. If the child is in immediate danger, has life-threatening injury, or contact is lost before safety is established, use 999 and the approved emergency handover or welfare-check procedure. Exact reporting, consent, confidentiality, documentation, destination, and disconnect actions remain GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED.
Call Back If: immediate danger or unsafe caregiver; uncontrolled bleeding, collapse, or serious injury; caller disconnects before safety is established.

advice.Title: First aid for a clearly minor scrape
Content: Only when injury and safeguarding concerns are absent, wash hands, rinse the surface with clean running water, pat the surrounding skin dry, and cover with a clean non-stick dressing. Change it if wet or dirty. Do not use harsh chemicals in the wound. Medicine, antibiotic, and tetanus advice require age, pregnancy, allergy, immunization, and local-policy checks.
Call Back If: bleeding restarts or will not stop; increasing redness, swelling, warmth, pain, pus, red streaking, or fever; movement, feeling, or colour changes; safeguarding concern develops.

references: NHS.UK, "Cuts and grazes", https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cuts-and-grazes/ (page last reviewed 02 April 2026)
NICE, "Child maltreatment: when to suspect maltreatment in under 18s", https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg89/chapter/recommendations
